reasoning: The exact contribution — ASR as a function of the number of sampling attempts N under best-of-N (repeated sampling) attacks, per model — is the central result of "Best-of-N Jailbreaking" (Hughes et al., arXiv 2412.03556, NeurIPS 2025). That paper establishes that ASR@N follows a predictable power law across models and modalities, plots these curves, and even forecasts ASR at large N from small N. Critically for this proposal, BoN includes a temperature-only resampling baseline with NO augmentation (resampling 500 responses at temperature 1 vs 0 on HarmBench), which is precisely the plain stochastic-sampling setup proposed here, and the harness/codebase is already public (jplhughes.github.io/bon-jailbreaking). Follow-up work (e.g. "Statistical Estimation of Adversarial Risk under Best-of-N Sampling," arXiv 2601.22636; "Quantifying LLM Safety Degradation Under Repeated Attacks," arXiv 2605.12869) further studies the N-to-success budget and survival curves. The proposal's only differences are minor and incremental: StrongREJECT prompts instead of HarmBench, capping N at 64, and packaging a deployer-facing reproducible tool.

evidence.title: Best-of-N Jailbreaking (Hughes, Price, Lynch et al.)
evidence.summary: Core paper: ASR as a function of number of samples N follows a power law across models and modalities; plots ASR@N curves; forecasts ASR at N=10,000 from N=1,000 with ~4.6% error. Includes a temperature-only resampling baseline WITHOUT augmentation on HarmBench (resample 500 responses at temp 1 vs 0), and uses StrongREJECT-style scoring. Public codebase at jplhughes.github.io/bon-jailbreaking. Directly delivers the proposed ASR@N-per-model curves and reproducible harness.

evidence.title: Statistical Estimation of Adversarial Risk in Large Language Models under Best-of-N Sampling
evidence.summary: Follow-up that formalizes estimating attack risk as a function of N under best-of-N sampling, directly addressing the 'how many samples to reach a given success threshold' question the proposal poses.

evidence.title: Quantifying LLM Safety Degradation Under Repeated Attacks Using Survival Analysis
evidence.summary: Studies how cumulative jailbreak success grows with repeated attempts per model using survival curves, overlapping with the proposed 'N needed to cross 50% success' metric.

evidence.title: Best-of-N Jailbreaking (NeurIPS camera-ready)
evidence.summary: Peer-reviewed venue confirms credibility (Anthropic/MATS authors). Reports 53-71% of jailbreaks succeed within 100 samples on Claude/GPT, 22-30% on Gemini, demonstrating per-model ASR-vs-N budget analysis.

evidence.title: Jailbreak Foundry: From Papers to Runnable Attacks for Reproducible Evaluation
evidence.summary: Provides a unified reproducible harness with standardized ASR across attacks and victim models, covering the 'ship the harness so deployers can reproduce' goal.
